diff_user.system: You are optimizing a Go function. Popcount(xs []uint64) int must return the total number of set bits across all words of xs. Each candidate is scored by running it in giri, a Go SSA interpreter, on 50 test vectors. It must return the reference result on every vector, and leave xs unchanged. Among correct candidates, a lower abstract cost (the number of SSA instructions executed over all vectors) scores higher, and any correct candidate scores above any incorrect one. The only import allowed is math/bits. Keep the function's name and signature.
responses:
## Proposed change: add a 32-word unrolled loop before the existing 16-word block

The current program does one `OnesCount64` per word and pays loop overhead once per 16 words. Per-word work is already minimal (a load, a popcount, an add), so the remaining gains come from amortizing loop control and the reslice (`xs = xs[16:]`) over more words. A 32-word main loop halves that per-iteration overhead on large inputs.

The 32-word loop leaves at most 31 words. A single 16-word `if` handles one half-block, and the existing branch tree handles the final ≤15 words. The tree and the rest of the function are unchanged, so correctness is preserved: the sum is the same, and `xs` is not modified.

Risk: for short inputs the extra `if len(xs) >= 16` test adds a few instructions. The test vectors' length distribution is unknown, so this could be neutral or slightly negative there. The gain is concentrated on long inputs.
